audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings tell you to block Rupture with Aegis Assault — 'E to block his Q knockup line so the spike whiffs'. Aegis Assault blocks damage, not crowd control, and Rupture is not a line.
audit.why: Riot's Aegis Assault text: Pantheon 'becoming invulnerable to damage from the front' while striking repeatedly — the kit flags it as a channel any CC cancels. Riot's Rupture text: it 'ruptures the ground at target location, popping enemy units into the air'. So channelling into Rupture eats the knockup anyway, and the knockup ends the channel. The current advice tells you to hold still inside the one thing that punishes holding still.
audit.corrected: Never channel Aegis Assault into Rupture — the block stops the damage, not the knockup that cancels it. Rupture is 6s, so step off the telegraph instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream is called 'W silence' but nothing says what the silence costs you, and Carnivore is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Feral Scream is an 11s cone at 300 range that silences — with Shield Vault silenced you have no gap-closer and no stun for the duration, which is the whole reason his disengage works. Carnivore heals him health and mana on every unit killed, scaling with level, which is why poking a farming Cho'Gath achieves nothing.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream's 11s silence named as the Shield Vault lockout; Carnivore named as the reason chip poke does not stick.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and Feast is described as an 'execute' that 'ignores your squishy frame'.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60 and deals true damage — the point is not that you are squishy, it is that armour does nothing. Rupture 6s, Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Vorpal Spikes 8/7/6/5/4. Rupture at 6s against Shield Vault's 13s is the sequencing problem: you get one gap-close per two Ruptures.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in spikes, cooldown block, dos and donts; Feast reframed as true damage that invalidates armour, per _missing-interactions.json.

audit.why: FAV at 52.79% over 627 games with the chart giving Pantheon six of seven stages is right: Cho'Gath is a one-ability farmer through the levels Pantheon is strongest, and level 6 is the only 'Skill' row because Grand Starfall does not solve a health bar.

edits.after: Shield Vault's leap-stun into Q taps: at level 1-2 you out-stat a Cho'Gath with one ability, no kill threat, and Rupture on 6s.

edits.after: Cho'Gath's threat window: Feast stacks balloon his HP, and its true damage on an 80s cooldown ignores every point of armour you bought.

edits.before: Cho'Gath has nothing to fight you with at levels 1-3 — he's a one-ability farmer while you have point-and-click W-stun damage and Q poke. Use W to stun-engage, E to block his Q knockup line so the spike whiffs, then Q-tap and walk out before his silence cooldown is back. Avoid eating Q (knockup) into W (silence) stacked on top of each other — that's his only kill setup. This is your lane: every Feast stack he doesn't have is HP you can still burst through.
edits.after: Cho'Gath has nothing to fight you with at levels 1-3 — a one-ability farmer against Shield Vault's leap-stun and Comet Spear poke. W in, Q-tap, and walk out inside Feral Scream's 11 seconds. Do not answer Rupture with Aegis Assault: the shield blocks its damage from the front, but the knockup lands anyway and cancels your channel. Step off the telegraph instead. Every Feast stack he lacks is HP you can still burst.

edits.before: You're still ahead through 4-6 — empowered-Q poke chips him and your E cleanly eats his Q so he can't farm-poke you for free. At 6 your Grand Starfall isn't a 1v1 win button against a tank this chunky, so use it as a roam to snowball a sidelane or grab a pick elsewhere; trying to solo-kill a Feast-stacking Cho'Gath into his own R is a losing race. Bank the tempo, take plates, and force objectives while you still out-damage his health bar.
edits.after: You're still ahead through 4-6, but poke alone gets you nothing: Carnivore refunds him health and mana on every minion he kills. Win by forcing short W-stun trades between Feral Scream's 11s and dodging a 6s Rupture rather than channelling into it. At 6 Grand Starfall is not a 1v1 button against this health bar, so roam with it; racing a Feast-stacking Cho'Gath is a race you lose. Take plates and objectives instead.

edits.before: At level 1 you're one of the strongest champions in the game with point-and-click W-stun damage, while Cho'Gath has a single ability and zero kill threat back.
edits.after: At level 1 you are one of the strongest in the game with Shield Vault's 600-range leap-stun, while Cho'Gath has one ability and zero kill threat back.

edits.before: Level 3 with W-stun, Q-burst and E-block is your premier kill window — you delete him long before any Feast stacks exist.
edits.after: Level 3 with W-stun and Q-burst is your premier kill window — you delete him long before Feast has a single stack on it.

notes: The headline fix is that the page told you to answer Rupture with Aegis Assault in four separate places. That is the wrong button: the shield stops frontal damage, the knockup still lands, and any CC ends the channel — so the advised play converts a dodgeable 6s ability into a lost 22s cooldown plus a knockup. _missing-interactions.json's 'dash-denied' entry for Rupture is consistent with this (airborne locks out Shield Vault and Grand Starfall) and I wrote the channel half, which Riot's own text supports directly. Carnivore was absent from the entire matchup despite being the reason poke does not stick to a farming Cho'Gath.
